title: Run credential call
description: The body of the control plane's call with the path run-credential, a POST of application/json to the adapter's call_url followed by run-credential (adapter.schema.json), signed as definitions.schema.json describes a call: an access credential for one run, for the resources, at the access level access, for the purpose purpose, under one grant: for a call whose purpose is harness, the grant grant_ref; for a call whose purpose is work, which has no grant_ref, a grant of the connection connection_id. A call whose purpose is work contains connection_id, the connection of the collections of the resources, as the control plane holds it for the run's organisation, which is a live connection of that organisation when the call is sent. A call has one connection_id, so all resources of a call are collections of one connection. The adapter checks that each collection whose ref is a resource is a live collection under connection_id in its state, and does not look the connection up from a ref. It uses only a grant that the control plane's copy of grants has under connection_id (grants.schema.json: GET /v1/grants and the grant entries of the change feed) that covers each collection and allows the access level access, and never a grant of another connection. It never uses a grant that it keeps only while it sends that grant's report again (grants.schema.json). For a call whose purpose is harness, grant_ref and each resource are the grant_ref and the resource_ref of a resolve result, as the adapter answered them, never its public_ref (resolve-answer.schema.json). A call whose purpose is harness has access read, and the schema refuses any other access for it. The control plane uses a credential from a call whose purpose is harness only with access read, and checks whether a run may use the credential each time it uses the credential for a run, not once when the credential was minted. The rules depend on the call that the credential came from. A credential from a call made for a run of the grant's organisation, under a grant of a live connection of the run's organisation, is used only for runs of that organisation, including a credential under credential_scope grant that covers every resource of the grant. A credential from a call made for an assignment is used only for runs of the organisation of that assignment, and only to read the assigned source. A run that may use a grant only through an assignment uses only a credential of the second kind, from a call made for that assignment, with credential_scope resource and resources set to the resource_ref of the assigned source alone; under credential_scope grant, such a run gets no harness credential and reads the assigned source only with the call with the path read. The adapter answers a signed 200 with run-credential-answer.schema.json, or refuses with refusal.schema.json, in this order: 409 grant_unknown, for a call with grant_ref, the adapter holds no grant grant_ref; 403 resource_not_covered, the grant does not cover one of the resources, or, for a call whose purpose is work, a collection of the call is not a live collection under connection_id in the adapter's state, or no grant of that connection in the control plane's copy of grants covers one of the collections, or the paths of the resources do not fit in the answer (run-credential-answer.schema.json), or the filled paths overlap on one host (description.schema.json, $defs.apply); 403 access_not_granted, the grant does not allow access for the resources, such as write under a grant that allows read alone, or, for a call whose purpose is work, a grant of that connection covers each collection and none allows the access level access; 503 source_unavailable, the source did not answer or was busy, and the control plane may send the call again later, built anew. How far one credential reaches is the description's credential_scope (description.schema.json). A call whose purpose is work has 1 to 250 resources in resources with the access read, and exactly one with the access write. A resource is the ref of a collection, exactly as the adapter wrote it as ref in its listing of collections (source-collections.schema.json) and as collection_ref in its listing of items (source-items.schema.json); when a target came from an item, that collection is the item's collection. A resource is not a resource_ref of a resolve result. The answer to a call with several resources is one credential: its apply items list the path of each resource. The answer has at most 512 paths (run-credential-answer.schema.json). An adapter covers N resources only when N × p + c ≤ 512. Here p is the number of path entries that one resource adds across all apply items. c is the number of paths that belong to no single resource, such as a template without {target.path}. It covers fewer when paths of different items cannot share one list of 32. It refuses a call over its limit with 403 resource_not_covered. A call whose purpose is harness has 1 to 64 resources. The adapter refuses a call whose time is more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, or whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401; definitions.schema.json has the replay rule. The adapter has one access key for every organisation, and no call but a call with the path run-credential whose purpose is work contains a connection_id, so a resolve result can contain a grant_ref of a connection of another organisation. The control plane uses a resolve result only under a grant that the run may use: a grant of a live connection of the run's organisation; or, only to read a harness source and only with access read, a grant whose organisation assigned that source to the run's organisation, at that version and at that path or export. The control plane also uses a result with public: true without a grant, and then only to read the resource with the call with the path read-public, with the result's public_ref as resource_ref (read-public.schema.json). Under an assignment, the control plane sends a call with the path run-credential only when the credential_scope of the adapter's description is resource, which it also is when absent (description.schema.json), and with resources set to the resource_ref of the assigned source alone; when credential_scope is grant, the control plane sends no call with the path run-credential under an assignment, and reads the assigned source only with the call with the path read. A harness source is a remote source that the run's harness extends or takes a module from, whether that harness is the harness file of the target or the harness member of the run documents (run/v1 documents.schema.json). An assignment never covers a call with the path run-credential whose purpose is work or whose access is write: work access comes only from a grant of a live connection of the run's organisation. The control plane treats every other resolve result as covered: false, or, when the result has public: true, as a result with public: true and no grant_ref, so nothing that a run of one organisation receives shows that another organisation holds a grant for that address. The control plane sends a call with the path read, and a call with the path run-credential whose purpose is harness, only under a grant that the run may use, and sends a call with the path run-credential whose purpose is work only with the connection_id of the collections of the call's resources, which is a live connection of the run's organisation when the call is sent. The control plane sends a call with the path read-public only with resource_ref set to the public_ref of a resolve result with public: true, never with the resource_ref of a covered result, and never sends a call with the path run-credential for a resource that it reads with the call with the path read-public: reading a public resource gives the run no credential. An access token covers its resources at every version and at every path, so an assignment of one version and one path or export still lets the run read the whole resource with the access token. The adapter ignores a member that this schema does not define, unless the must_understand of the body lists it. It refuses a call whose must_understand lists a pointer that it does not define, 400 invalid_request. A writer sends no key or secret in a member that this contract does not define.

version.description: The document format. The adapter refuses a version it does not read.

time.description: When the control plane built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. The adapter refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, with an unsigned 401.

grant_ref.description: The grant the credential is minted under, as the adapter reported it (grant.schema.json). Present exactly when the purpose is harness. A call whose purpose is work has no grant_ref: the adapter uses a grant that the control plane's copy of grants has under connection_id, that covers the collection and allows the access level access, and never a grant of another connection.

connection_id.description: The connection of the collections of the resources, as the control plane holds it for the run's organisation (definitions.schema.json, connection_id), which is a live connection of that organisation when the call is sent. Present exactly when the purpose is work. The adapter checks that each collection whose ref is a resource is a live collection under connection_id in its state, and does not look the connection up from a ref. It uses only a grant that the control plane's copy of grants has under connection_id (grants.schema.json: GET /v1/grants and the grant entries of the change feed) that covers each collection and allows the access level access, and never a grant of another connection. It never uses a grant that it keeps only while it sends that grant's report again (grants.schema.json).

resources.description: The resources the credential covers, none twice, 1 to 250. For the purpose harness, 1 to 64, each the resource_ref of a resolve result, as the adapter answered it, never its public_ref. For the purpose work, 1 to 250 with the access read and exactly one with the access write: each the ref of a collection, exactly as the adapter wrote it as ref in its listing of collections (source-collections.schema.json) and as collection_ref in its listing of items (source-items.schema.json); when a target came from an item, that collection is the item's collection. The paths of the answer limit how many resources one call covers (run-credential-answer.schema.json).

access.description: read for the purpose harness; read or write for the purpose work: the access level the run has on the resources. For a call whose purpose is work, read for a run whose documents have the access write-no-push, and the access of the run's documents otherwise (run/v1 documents.schema.json). A call for places that the run only reads, such as read_targets of the run documents, has the access read.

purpose.description: harness, a credential the run uses to fetch what composes its harness; or work, a credential the run uses for its work on the resources.

must_understand.description: The members of the document that the reader must understand, each as a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) counted from the document, such as /purpose. List each once, at most 32. A pointer has no line feed, and writes ~ only as ~0 or ~1. Each pointer is to a member that this schema defines. The adapter ignores a member that this schema does not define, unless the must_understand of the body lists it. It refuses a call whose must_understand lists a pointer that it does not define, 400 invalid_request.
